## Probability, randomness, and Live’s MIDI tools

**1. “Take a Chance: Producing with Probability in Live 11” – Ableton Blog**  
URL: `https://www.ableton.com/en/blog/take-chance-producing-probability-live-11/`  

- Technique: Shows how to use **Note Chance** and **Velocity Chance** in Live’s MIDI editor to introduce controlled randomness into patterns—e.g., setting **Note Chance to 50%** so each note has a 50% probability of playing, and using **velocity ranges** so each trigger gets a randomized velocity within a defined min–max.[https://www.ableton.com/en/blog/take-chance-producing-probability-live-11/]

This article is directly about generative / probabilistic workflows and is highly relevant to repetitive, evolving patterns in techno and ambient.

---

## Core MIDI Chance / Random tools (manual & FAQ)

These are not “One Thing” blog posts, but official Ableton documentation that concretely define the parameters you’re asking about.

**2. “Note and Velocity Chance in Live 11 FAQ” – Ableton Help**  
URL: `https://help.ableton.com/hc/en-us/articles/360019144299-Note-and-Velocity-Chance-in-Live-11-FAQ`  

- Technique: Explains how **Note Chance** determines if a MIDI note plays based on a percentage setting from **0% to 100%** (e.g. 50% = half the time), and how **Velocity Chance** defines a *velocity range* within which each note’s velocity is randomized when triggered.[https://help.ableton.com/hc/en-us/articles/360019144299-Note-and-Velocity-Chance-in-Live-11-FAQ]  
- Concrete workflow: You open the **Notes/Samples** tab, click the **Chance** icon, select notes, and drag the Chance marker to set the probability per note; for Velocity Chance, you click **Velocity**, select notes, then hold **CMD/Ctrl while dragging** to set the randomized velocity range.[https://help.ableton.com/hc/en-us/articles/360019144299-Note-and-Velocity-Chance-in-Live-11-FAQ]

There are localized versions with the same information in Spanish, French, and German:  
- Spanish FAQ: `https://help.ableton.com/hc/es/articles/360019144299-Preguntas-frecuentes-sobre-el-azar-Chance-de-notas-y-velocidades`[https://help.ableton.com/hc/es/articles/360019144299-Preguntas-frecuentes-sobre-el-azar-Chance-de-notas-y-velocidades]  
- French FAQ: `https://help.ableton.com/hc/fr-fr/articles/360019144299-FAQ-Note-Chance-et-Velocity-Chance`[https://help.ableton.com/hc/fr-fr/articles/360019144299-FAQ-Note-Chance-et-Velocity-Chance]  
- German FAQ: `https://help.ableton.com/hc/de/articles/360019144299-Noten-und-Velocity-Chance-FAQ`[https://help.ableton.com/hc/de/articles/360019144299-Noten-und-Velocity-Chance-FAQ]

**3. Live MIDI Effect Reference – Live 11 & Live 12 manuals**  
Live 11 MIDI effects: `https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/11/live-midi-effect-reference/`[https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/11/live-midi-effect-reference/]  
Live 12 MIDI effects: `https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-midi-effect-reference/`[https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-midi-effect-reference/]  

- Technique: Defines **Chance** and **Velocity** parameters for MIDI effects that generate notes. For example, **Velocity** is a *relative* control from **1%–200%**, where **100%** preserves the incoming velocity, and **Chance** sets the probability from **0%–100%** that a generated note will play when an incoming note is received.[https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-midi-effect-reference/]  
- Random device detail: For the **Random** MIDI effect, the manual explains that **Chance** acts like a “dry/wet control for randomness”: the **Choices** parameter sets how many distinct random shifts are possible, and **Scale × Choices** defines the possible pitch offsets relative to the incoming note.[https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/11/live-midi-effect-reference/]

These references are the most concrete sources for generative sequencing based on MIDI effects and probability in Live.

## Note/Velocity/Random MIDI effects (non‑blog but relevant technique)

While I cannot see a specific “One Thing” blog post dedicated to Note/Velocity/Random right now, the following sources provide usable techniques:

**4. “10. Editing MIDI Notes and Velocities” – Live 11 Manual**  
URL: `https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/11/editing-midi-notes-and-velocities/`  

- Technique: In the **Velocity Editor** lane you set a **Randomize Range** slider and click the **Randomize** button, which randomizes velocities of selected notes within that range—very useful for humanizing repetitive patterns while staying inside a defined dynamic band.[https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/11/editing-midi-notes-and-velocities/]  
- You can similarly randomize **Chance** values in the **Chance Editor** lane for selected notes, turning a rigid loop into a probabilistic, evolving pattern.[https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/11/editing-midi-notes-and-velocities/]

**5. Ableton Forum thread on Random / Velocity MIDI effects**  
URL: `https://forum.ableton.com/viewtopic.php?t=224225`  

- Technique: Users describe stacking **Random MIDI Effects** in chains inside a **MIDI Effect Rack**; each chain has different Random settings, and key zones decide which notes get randomized. This creates generative melodic variation from a single input clip.[https://forum.ableton.com/viewtopic.php?t=224225]  
- They also note using **Velocity** devices at the end of a chain to constrain or override the resulting velocities from randomization.[https://forum.ableton.com/viewtopic.php?t=224225]

This is not official blog content, but it’s a concrete workflow around the Random device and repetition.

---

## LFO device tricks & movement

I don’t currently have direct access to specific Ableton “One Thing” articles on the LFO device, but one relevant tutorial and some general guidance are available.

**6. “One Tip: Using Ableton’s LFO To Give Your Tracks More Movement” – YouTube tutorial**  
URL: `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ORC4fWQoMBg`  

- Technique: Demonstrates mapping Ableton’s **LFO device** to parameters such as **dry/wet of an effect** to add constant, subtle movement; in the video, the LFO’s **Map** button is used to assign modulation to an effect, then rate and depth are tuned for rhythmic motion.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ORC4fWQoMBg]

**7. “LFO in Ableton — Quick Guide” – Epica Labs (third‑party)**  
URL: `https://epicalab.com/lfo-in-ableton/`  

- Technique: Step‑by‑step guide: load **LFO** (or Max for Live LFO), click **Map Mode**, select a target parameter (filter cutoff, wavetable position, pitch, volume), then choose **sync vs free rate**, waveform, and set moderate modulation depth as a starting point.[https://epicalab.com/lfo-in-ableton/]  
- Suggested workflow: Use **tempo‑sync** for rhythmic techno repetition, and **free‑running LFO** with slow rates for generative ambient drift.[https://epicalab.com/lfo-in-ableton/]

I cannot currently provide an Ableton “One Thing” blog URL specifically on LFO, but this YouTube tutorial and the Epica Labs guide offer the same type of device‑level technique.
